title: Wellness 2.0: When It's All Too Much

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: In 1906, the journalist Upton Sinclair published The Jungle,
sentences.zh: 1906年，记者厄普顿·辛克莱出版了《屠场》一书，

sentences.en: a novel based on his undercover reporting in Chicago's meatpacking plants.
sentences.zh: 这是一部基于他在芝加哥肉类加工厂卧底调查经历而创作的小说。

sentences.en: The book tells a story of a young couple, Yorgis and Ona,
sentences.zh: 书中讲述了一对年轻夫妇——约吉斯和奥娜的故事，

sentences.en: who immigrate to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们与亲戚一起，

sentences.en: from Lithuania along with their relatives.
sentences.zh: 从立陶宛移民到了美国。

sentences.en: The optimism they feel about their new country is soon tested.
sentences.zh: 他们对这个新国家怀有的乐观情绪很快就受到了考验。

sentences.en: Family members find jobs at a meatpacking plant,
sentences.zh: 家人们在一家肉类加工厂找到了工作，

sentences.en: but the work is dangerous and pays little.
sentences.zh: 但工作既危险，报酬又微薄。

sentences.en: The family suffers illness and injuries.
sentences.zh: 这个家庭饱受疾病和伤痛的折磨。

sentences.en: Work is tenuous, with periodic wage cuts,
sentences.zh: 工作极不稳定，不仅经常减薪，

sentences.en: poor benefits, and seasonal layoffs.
sentences.zh: 福利待遇也很差，还面临季节性裁员。

sentences.en: The family is evicted from their home
sentences.zh: 一家人被房东赶了出来，

sentences.en: and moves to a crowded, dirty boarding house.
sentences.zh: 搬进了一间拥挤、肮脏的寄宿公寓。

sentences.en: Unable to afford a doctor,
sentences.zh: 因为付不起医药费，

sentences.en: Ona dies in childbirth, as does her baby.
sentences.zh: 奥娜在分娩时去世了，孩子也没能活下来。

sentences.en: When Yorgis and Ona's remaining son dies as well,
sentences.zh: 当约吉斯和奥娜剩下的那个儿子也夭折后，

sentences.en: Yorgis slides into alcoholism.
sentences.zh: 约吉斯陷入了酗酒的深渊。

sentences.en: Upton Sinclair wrote The Jungle with the aim of awakening the conscience of Americans
sentences.zh: 厄普顿·辛克莱写《屠场》的初衷是唤醒美国人的良知，

sentences.en: to the desperate conditions of the working poor.
sentences.zh: 让他们关注贫困劳动者绝望的生存状况。

sentences.en: He hoped to spark a movement that would reform the nation's labor laws.
sentences.zh: 他希望借此引发一场改革国家劳动法的运动。

sentences.en: But the public did not respond the way he expected.
sentences.zh: 但公众的反应却并非如他所愿。

sentences.en: Readers did care about the quality of the meat they ate,
sentences.zh: 读者们确实关心他们所吃肉类的质量，

sentences.en: but seemed indifferent to the plight of exploited workers.
sentences.zh: 却似乎对被剥削工人的苦难漠不关心。

sentences.en: Journalists, activists, and leaders often get frustrated
sentences.zh: 记者、活动家和领导者常常会感到沮丧，

sentences.en: when their best effort to draw attention to a cause
sentences.zh: 因为他们为引起对某项事业的关注所做的最大努力，

sentences.en: does not prompt people to get off their couches and take action.
sentences.zh: 却没能促使人们从沙发上站起来采取行动。

sentences.en: Sometimes, this is because people feel apathetic.
sentences.zh: 有时，这是因为人们感到冷漠。

sentences.en: They don't know how to respond
sentences.zh: 他们不知道该如何应对，

sentences.en: or assume any efforts they make will go nowhere.
sentences.zh: 或者认为自己所做的任何努力都无济于事。

sentences.en: Other times, it's because they feel overwhelmed
sentences.zh: 另一些时候，是因为他们感到不知所措，

sentences.en: or consumed with paralyzing guilt.
sentences.zh: 或者被瘫痪般的内疚感所吞噬。

sentences.en: Whatever the driver,
sentences.zh: 无论驱动因素是什么，

sentences.en: when it comes to existential issues such as climate change or war,
sentences.zh: 当涉及到气候变化或战争这类生存议题时，

sentences.en: inaction can have terrible consequences.
sentences.zh: 不作为可能会带来可怕的后果。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we continue our New Year's series, Wellness 2.0.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，我们将继续我们的新年系列节目——“健康2.0”。

sentences.en: We'll look at how we come to feel disengaged and burned out, even on topics we might care about,
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨我们是如何变得消极怠工和精疲力竭的，即使是对我们可能关心的议题也是如此，

sentences.en: and how we can begin to retrieve our sense of efficacy and purpose.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何开始找回我们的效能感和目标感。

sentences.en: Many problems we face are easy to solve.
sentences.zh: 我们面临的许多问题都很容易解决。

sentences.en: A missing ingredient for a recipe, a burned-out light bulb, a parking ticket.
sentences.zh: 食谱里少了一种配料、灯泡烧坏了、收到一张停车罚单。

sentences.en: We make short work of these problems, briskly crossing them off our to-do lists.
sentences.zh: 我们能迅速处理这些问题，利落地把它们从待办事项清单上划掉。

sentences.en: But modern life also seems full of issues that researchers call wicked problems, challenges
sentences.zh: 但现代生活似乎也充满了研究人员所说的“棘手问题”，这些挑战

sentences.en: so huge, complicated, and intractable that they defy our attempts to solve them.
sentences.zh: 如此巨大、复杂且难以处理，以至于它们超出了我们解决问题的能力。

sentences.en: When we come up against problems like these, we tend to respond differently.
sentences.zh: 当我们遇到这类问题时，我们的反应往往不同。

sentences.en: At California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt, Sarah Jacket-Ray studies how we
sentences.zh: 在加州州立理工大学洪堡分校，莎拉·杰克特-雷研究我们

sentences.en: respond to huge, overwhelming problems, and how we can get better at dealing with them.
sentences.zh: 如何应对巨大且令人不知所措的问题，以及我们如何能更好地处理它们。

sentences.en: I sat in a rocking chair, munching, and then, hours later, after darkness fell, I walked out into a great tumble of stars.

sentences.en: Although I was alone in my silent cell, I didn't feel alone.
sentences.zh: 虽然我独自待在安静的修道室里，但我并不感到孤独。
